axes.model_access:
**It calls no model itself** — an interface implementation called by MCP clients. It wraps MongoDB database operations
(connecting, collection queries, aggregations) and Atlas management as tools for agents.
axes.runtime:
A local process (npx stdio); GitHub 1,146★, last push 2026-10-21 (API verified).
The official docs/mcp page direct-fetched 404 — the current official line is the repo itself (direct-fetch verified 2026-10-21).
axes.local_files: Reads and writes no local project files — the scope is database instances (a local mongod or an Atlas cluster both count as its targets).
axes.background: stdio lives and dies with the client; no background-task semantics.
axes.tools:
Connect/list databases and collections, find/aggregate/insert/update/delete, Atlas cluster management, etc.;
write capabilities are complete. The complete inventory follows the repo README.
axes.context: No cross-session memory — data state lives in the database itself.
axes.permissions:
**Two credential routes**: a connection string direct connection (whatever database it can reach = whatever it can do, including writes/deletes) or an Atlas API key (the Atlas management surface).
The official README explicitly notes a confirmation mechanism for high-risk operations (delete-class tools carry a confirmation parameter) —
but the boundary is still the credential: before hooking up an agent, defend on the assumption "it can drop collections".
axes.fit:
Fits: agent dev flows for MongoDB projects (inspect schemas, run aggregations, try write operations).
Not a fit: hard read-only sandboxes; non-MongoDB stacks.

mcp.transport: **stdio** (npx starts a local process). Verified: repo README (fetched directly 2026-10-21).
mcp.auth:
Two routes: connection string (mongodb:// direct to an instance) or Atlas API credentials;
the support surface of read-only connection options not verified item by item.
mcp.scope:
Read surface: list databases/collections, find/aggregate; write surface: insert/update/delete, Atlas cluster management.
Delete-class tools carry a confirmation parameter (official README wording); no separate approval layer.

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/mcp/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/mcp/_protocol.md).
unknowns:
- The support surface of read-only connection options (not verified item by item)
- The complete Atlas tool inventory (not enumerated item by item)
- Whether the docs/mcp official page will come back (no statement seen — only the 404 fact is recorded)
related: Both database-class servers: Supabase works through its own BaaS project surface, MongoDB through the connection-string direct-to-instance surface.
